messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: High error rate + latency on /v1/generate (us-west-2). Alerting SRE oncall. Please acknowledge if you're taking this.
Miguel Ramos: I got the page, jumping in now. Can someone drop the war room link? I'll take incident owner for initial triage. @Sanaa please help with customer impact assessment.
Sanaa Patel: Acknowledged. War room: https://warroom.internal/r/incident-230500 (have it pinned). Initial checks: error spikes at 07:12:03 UTC, 5xx% up to ~18% and p95 latency from 120ms -> 2.4s for short prompts.
Chris Lee: Confirming logs show a surge of 502s from the inference gateway -> model-proxy group. Rolling logs now. `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=model-proxy -o wide` shows 2/5 pods in CrashLoopBackOff.
Miguel Ramos: Thanks. Oncall checklist: 1) scale model-proxy to 8 replicas 2) check model GPU pool utilization 3) failover to fallback variant if backend errors persist. I'll run scale now.
Alex Morgan: Scaling executed: `kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy -n inference --replicas=8` — started. Also creating a temporary routing rule to reduce burst to dedicated pools.
Sanaa Patel: Customer impact: Preliminary - customers in us-west-2 may see failed generations or long hangs. No evidence of data exfiltration. Recommending status page: "Degraded performance and errors for text generation in US-West (ongoing)."
Miguel Ramos: Observability: adding trace sample to the war room for 07:11-07:20 UTC. Checkouts: model-proxy logs show OOMKilled on a couple nodes, but most are crash loops due to `connection reset by peer` from redis-kv cache.
Chris Lee: I'm spinning up extra cache replicas and tainting the problematic nodes: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-7` then `kubectl drain ip-10-0-4-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Moving traffic off.
Eva Chen: FYI I'm drafting status updates and customer emails, will paste drafts here for review.
pm-liaison-bot: @channel Suggested statuspage entry (draft): "We are investigating increased errors and latency for text generation in US-West. Impact: a subset of API requests may fail or be delayed. Mitigation in progress. ETA unknown. Updates every 15 minutes." Reaction: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sanaa Patel: Good. Customer notification (short): "We're investigating an issue impacting text generation for customers in US-West. Some requests may fail or be slow. We're working to restore normal service and will share updates shortly. — Redwood Inference Ops"
Alex Morgan: After scale, p95 latency dropped from 2.4s -> 600ms; error rate reduced to ~6%. Still above baseline. Proceeding to roll traffic to fallback model variant (quantized v2) for high-latency customers.
Miguel Ramos: Approved. Execute gradual rollout: update routing policy for latency-sensitive routes to fallback-model-v2 with 25% traffic.
Alex Morgan: `redwoodctl route update --service generate --region us-west-2 --fallback-model fallback-model-v2 --weight 25%` — applied.
Chris Lee: Observing connection errors dropping. Error rate down to ~2.3%, p95 420ms. Cache replicas up.
Miguel Ramos: Good. Prepare postmortem skeleton: cause (cache node instability + OOM), mitigation (scale + cordon + fallback routing), customer impact summary, and follow-ups (increase cache replica autoscaling, improve OOM safeguards). Assigning owners: caching follow-up -> Chris, routing/fallback docs -> Alex, postmortem write -> Sanaa.
Sanaa Patel: I'll draft the postmortem and the customer-facing timeline. Adding immediate action: suspend any large batch jobs scheduled in us-west-2 for next 2 hours.
Eva Chen: Statuspage update ready to publish, two-line message + link to war room. Proposed internal comms template for customers who ask for details (sensitive):

"We experienced elevated errors and elevated latency for text generation in US-West due to transient instability in our caching layer causing connection resets to inference proxies. We mitigated by scaling proxies, replacing unhealthy cache nodes, and routing a portion of traffic to a robust fallback model (quantized variant). Normal service is being restored and we are monitoring. We'll follow up with a detailed timeline and root cause analysis." 

LMK edits.
Miguel Ramos: That reads fine. Post the statuspage message once we confirm error rate <3% for 5 minutes. Can someone confirm once stable for 5min? I'll stay on until handoff.
Chris Lee: Confirmed stable window starting 07:27:30 UTC. Keeping watch.
Alex Morgan: Monitoring dashboards look stable. Errors hovering ~1.5% and decreasing. Will set alert threshold tighter to catch regressions.
pm-liaison-bot: Suggested customer escalation note (for paid customers): "We are prioritizing your traffic to fallback routing and have engineers engaged. If you have urgent requests, reply to this message or open a support ticket and we'll escalate." Reaction: :email:
Sanaa Patel: Preparing final short update for customers. Draft: "Update 07:35 UTC: We have implemented mitigations and are seeing traffic return to normal levels. Some customers may still see intermittent failures; full resolution expected soon. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a detailed incident report." Agree?
Miguel Ramos: Agree. Eva, please post the statuspage and send the customer update. I'll create the incident channel summary and assign follow-ups.
Eva Chen: Posted to statuspage and sent coordinated emails to affected customers at 07:36 UTC. Copy of email saved in war room.
Miguel Ramos: Handoff plan: I will remain as owner for next 30 minutes. If everything remains stable I'll hand to Eva at 08:05 UTC for monitoring and postmortem prep. If regression happens, page SRE oncall.
Eva Chen: Acknowledged. I'll take the follow-up owner for postmortem and customer comms after the handoff. Preparing the timeline doc now.
Chris Lee: One last note — recommended action items for follow-up: increase cache liveness probes, add backpressure on batch ingestion, enforce mem limits on model-proxy containers. Logging more context around connection resets.
Miguel Ramos: Adding those to the follow-up list. Thanks all. Closing war room when postmortem skeleton is in the shared doc. Leaving handoff note in case anyone else needs context.
Eva Chen: Handoff done at 08:05 UTC. Miguel stepping out. I'll continue with postmortem and customer timeline. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident resolved (monitoring). If errors recur, new pager will be created.
